To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Internet of Things poses new requirements for the development of interactive applications and, consequently, new challenges for EUD approaches.

EUD for the Internet of Things requires: (1) a new set of design concepts to address dynamic, distributed, and heterogeneous contexts; and (2) a new set tools to support the development of applications that adapt to these new contexts.
the Internet of Things requires a shift in EUD approaches, from the current paradigm of programming by example to a more complex one, which we call programming by example and context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding and supporting end user development of Internet of Things applications.
the development of new tools to support end user development of applications in the Internet of Things era, and to support the design of new applications.
the design and development issues of EUD tools for the IoT, and the analysis of their design space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EUD in the context of the Internet of things is still an open research challenge.

the design space proposed in this paper can be used as a basis to understand and compare the main features that characterize the design of environments supporting end user development of applications in the Internet of Things era.
the Internet of Things has the potential to change the nature of EUD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EUD community is well positioned to address the challenges of the IoT and to provide tools to empower users in this context.
the Internet of Things calls for new approaches to end user development that are able to support the development of applications that adapt to dynamic contexts.
EUD can play an important role in supporting the development of Internet of Things applications, but that the current EUD research community has to address some important research challenges.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of environments for EUD in the Internet of Things should consider the following features: (i) a programming model that is easy to understand, (ii) a set of abstractions to support the creation of applications, (iii) an environment that allows for the integration of existing services and devices, (iv) a way of dealing with the dynamicity of the environment, and (v) a mechanism for the sharing of the created applications.
the Internet of Things calls for the design of new EUD environments, which should be able to cope with the dynamicity of such a technological setting.
the design space can be a useful tool for the community to identify the key concepts and the main issues that need to be addressed to support EUD in the context of the Internet of things.
